Three pieces, one from each of List A (faster, agile), List B (lyrical, expressive) and List C (varied styles/traditions); the repertoire lists are the same as for Performance Grades. At G1-3 some or all pieces may use woodwind accompaniment: DUET pieces (play upper part), DUET/PIANO either. Up to two unaccompanied SOLO pieces may be played. Some grades (e.g. Descant G2, G4; Flute G2, G3, G4, G6, G8; Oboe G1, G4, G6, G8; Clarinet G7; Bassoon G3; Sax G1, G2, G4) require at least one accompanied piece. Three pieces, one from each of List A (faster, agile), List B (lyrical, expressive) and List C (varied styles/traditions); the repertoire lists are the same as for Performance Grades. Live piano accompaniment required unless the piece is a solo/study; recorded accompaniment not allowed. At G1-3 some or all pieces may use woodwind accompaniment: DUET pieces (play upper part), DUET/PIANO either. Up to two unaccompanied SOLO pieces may be played. Some grades (e.g. Descant G2, G4; Flute G2, G3, G4, G6, G8; Oboe G1, G4, G6, G8; Clarinet G7; Bassoon G3; Sax G1, G2, G4) require at least one accompanied piece. May play from memory (examiner needs a copy). Related-instrument options: Descant may play one piece on tenor or treble recorder (then A/B/C lists still apply); Treble G1-5 may play one piece on descant, G6-8 on another recorder where indicated; Saxophones may play one piece (any list) on another saxophone; Flute G8 one piece on alto flute and Oboe G8 one on cor anglais where indicated. Pieces from the 2022 syllabus allowed until 31 Dec 2026 (all requirements from the same syllabus).

For G6, 7 or 8 candidates must already hold ABRSM Grade 5 (or above) in Music Theory, or Practical Musicianship, or Grade 5 on any Practical Grades solo Jazz instrument (accepted alternatives listed on the ABRSM site). No other grade is a prerequisite for entry (no need to take grades in order).

Practical Grades are face-to-face exams; ABRSM also offers Performance Grades (separate qualifications focusing on a whole performance) using the same repertoire lists, and digital exams; marks cannot be transferred between Practical and Performance Grades, and using different pieces for both is recommended. Alternative tests exist for specific needs (blind/partially sighted: Braille memory or aural repetition for sight-reading; deaf/hearing-impaired: alternative aural tests).
sections: Scales & technical work

Sight-reading

c.12-16 bars; adds 9/8, 5/8, 5/4 and changes of time signature; triplet patterns; rit. then a tempo; swung style (Flute, Clarinet, Saxophone); tenor clef (Bassoon); new keys (majors; minors): E, A♭; f♯, c
Aural & other tests

Sing or play back the upper part of a 2-part phrase; sing a melody from score with piano accompaniment; identify perfect/imperfect cadence; questions on texture or structure plus another feature; clap rhythm of extract and state time

exams.syllabus: Trinity Woodwind & Jazz Woodwind syllabus. Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Face-to-face: 3 pieces x 22 (fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) = 66; technical work 14; supporting tests 20 (Initial-G5: any two of sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge, 10 each; G6-8: sight reading 10 + aural or improvisation 10); total 100. Pass 60-74, Merit 75-86, Distinction 87-100 (Below Pass 1: 45-59; Below Pass 2: 0-44). Per piece: Distinction 19-22, Merit 16-18, Pass 13-15. No need to pass every section. Digital technical-work pathway: 3 pieces x 22 = 66, technical work 14, overall performance 20 (=100); digital Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x 25 = 100; same attainment bands. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (Pass/Merit/Distinction).

Three pieces from the current repertoire list: two accompanied from Group A and one unaccompanied from Group B. At Initial-G3 one Group A piece may be a duet (upper part; duet part on a woodwind instrument, live or recorded). Own composition may replace a piece (accompanied -> Group A, unaccompanied -> Group B), comparable in demand (Initial 0.5-1 min up to G8 3.5-5 min; stave notation required G6-8; no marks for quality of composition). Flute, clarinet and saxophone candidates may swap one piece for a Jazz Woodwind piece listed for the same instrument, grade and group. Instrument rules: piccolo/alto flute, Eb/bass clarinet, cor anglais, contrabassoon only where listed (max one such piece); recorder G6-8 must play both descant and treble, only one piece on tenor/sopranino/bass; no plastic saxophones. Repeats over 4 bars not played; da capo/dal segno observed; no metronomes; memory optional (no extra marks). Accompanist supplied by candidate; backing tracks allowed to G3 face-to-face (live from G4), and at all grades digitally.

Digital exams (filmed, one continuous take, up to 3GB) offer two pathways: Technical work (3 pieces + scales/arpeggios Set A or B, or exercises, or G6-8 orchestral extracts/study, + overall performance mark) or Repertoire-only (4 pieces: at least two Group A and one Group B, 25 marks each). Digital technical work uses the same material as face-to-face (Set A/B subsets); there are no supporting tests digitally.
sections: Scales & technical work

Scales & triads (from memory; examiner selects; digital: Set A or Set B): scales first five notes only of F major and G major, ascending and descending, tongued, mf, min crotchet=60; triads F major and G major, min quaver=120. (Digital Set A = F scale + G triad; Set B = G scale + F triad.)
Sight-reading
Unseen extract ~2 grades lower, 30 s preparation; range a 5th; keys (cumulative): F major.
Aural & other tests

Two of four tests (10 marks each): sight reading; aural; improvisation; musical knowledge. Aural (melody 4 bars, major key, 2 time, played by examiner): clap the pulse on the 3rd hearing; identify forte/piano; legato/staccato; highest or lowest of first three notes. Improvisation (stimulus of your choice): stylistic - 2-bar intro then 4 bars improvised once over piano, C major, chords I/V, march or lullaby; motivic - 2-bar fragment, response 4-6 bars, C major; harmonic - 4-bar sequence played once, I/V, C major. Musical knowledge: questions on your chosen pieces - pitch names, note durations, clefs/staves/barlines, key/time signatures, basic terms and signs.

p0011.d: Andersen's playful set of variations on a jaunty theme, here in Rampal's edition: each variation shows off a different trick, from rapid tonguing to sweeping arpeggios.

p0015.d: One of Arnold's short fantasies for solo wind: a compact sequence of contrasting moods, from wistful to playful, that tests tone, phrasing and characterisation without accompaniment.

p0022.d: Stallman's flute version of the grand Adagio that opens Bach's G minor solo violin sonata: richly ornamented, improvisatory lines that need sustained breath and shape.
p0022.rw: Noble music; hard to sustain on flute

p0023.d: The first two movements of Bach's E major flute sonata: a serene, ornamented slow introduction followed by a bright, dancing Allegro with flowing semiquavers.

p0027.d: The Allemande from Bach's solo flute partita: unbroken semiquavers with no written breaks, so the player must create phrasing and harmony while finding places to breathe.
p0027.rw: Iconic solo Bach; real breath-control test

p0041.d: The complete partita for solo flute: four dances (Allemande, Corrente, Sarabande, Bourrée angloise) demanding phrasing without breaks, wide leaps and implied harmony.
p0041.rw: Essential flute repertoire; deep musical payoff

p0042.d: The finale of the B minor sonata: a tightly argued fugue in quick tempo followed by a lively gigue, with intricate counterpoint shared with the keyboard.

p0050.d: C.P.E. Bach's unaccompanied flute sonata: an expressive, sighing Poco adagio, a restless Allegro and a lively finale, with dramatic leaps and sudden mood changes.

p0052.d: Bach's A major flute sonata with obbligato keyboard: a long first movement (partly reconstructed by editors), a tender Largo e dolce, and a joyful dancing finale.

p0053.d: Bach's largest flute sonata: a long, intricate opening Andante, a tender Largo e dolce and a fugal Presto finale, all written in true partnership with keyboard.

p0055.d: Bach's E minor sonata for flute and continuo: a brooding Adagio, two lively Allegros and an expressive Andante over a walking bass.

p0059.d: C.P.E. Bach's late 'Hamburg' sonata in G: a lilting Andante followed by a sparkling Rondo, in a light, elegant Classical style.

p0061.d: C.P.E. Bach's D major sonata for flute and obbligato keyboard: bright, extrovert outer movements framing an expressive slow movement.

p0064.d: Bach's complete E major flute sonata: four movements combining ornamented slow music, a dancing Allegro, a tender Siciliano and a lively finale.

p0079.d: A piece by jazz educator and composer David Baker; expect jazz-inflected rhythms and harmony, possibly with improvisatory character.

p0093.d: Paul Arma's flute arrangement of Bartók's Hungarian peasant songs: slow, haunting folk tunes followed by a lively chain of dances with bright, rustic energy.

p0132.d: An unaccompanied flute piece of rapid, soaring lines evoking birds in flight; fluid, virtuosic and modernist, with wide register and dynamic range.
p0132.rw: Brilliant modern solo; impressive when mastered

p0137.d: Landmark solo flute piece using proportional notation: rapid registral leaps, fragmented gestures and extreme dynamic contrasts create a sense of several voices.
p0137.rw: Iconic avant-garde work; formidable to bring off

p0138.d: Landmark solo flute piece using proportional notation: rapid registral leaps, fragmented gestures and extreme dynamic contrasts create a sense of several voices.
p0138.rw: Iconic avant-garde work; formidable to bring off

p0139.d: Lively closing movement of Berkeley's Flute Concerto: crisp, neoclassical writing with rhythmic bite and agile passagework.

p0142.d: Neoclassical three-movement sonatina, originally for treble recorder: clean lines, gentle wit and a lyrical slow movement in a clear, English idiom.

p0150.d: A French Baroque flute sonata in G minor, with graceful slow movements and lively dance-like quick ones; style and ornamentation are central.
p0150.rw: Elegant French Baroque; solid stylistic test

p0167.d: Brilliant 19th-century theme and variations by the inventor of the modern flute: a simple Alpine tune transformed with runs, leaps and fireworks.

p0168.d: Boehm's variations on Schubert's waltz 'Le Désir': an expressive introduction, the elegant theme, and increasingly brilliant variations.
p0168.rw: Brilliant salon piece; less often chosen

p0169.d: A dashing Romantic showpiece: an expressive introduction followed by a glittering polonaise with rapid runs, leaps and articulation fireworks.

p0171.d: Movement from Bolling's Suite for Flute and Jazz Piano Trio: a fugal, swinging piece blending Baroque counterpoint with jazz rhythms.

p0173.d: Borne's brilliant fantasy on Bizet's Carmen tunes, from the Habanera to the Toreador: a flute showpiece of runs, double tonguing and flair.

p0179.d: Boulez's early, explosive Sonatine for flute and piano: a dense single-movement serial work of violent contrasts, flutter-tonguing and rhythmic complexity.

p0181.d: A contemporary flute and piano piece by flautist Wissam Boustany: expressive and emotionally charged, using a modern sound palette.

p0184.d: York Bowen's flute sonata complete: richly Romantic English writing, from lyrical warmth to a brilliant, energetic finale.
p0184.rw: Rich, rewarding sonata; well-written for flute

p0185.d: An unaccompanied flute piece evoking Balinese gamelan: meditative, modal and atmospheric, with subtle colour and breath control.

p0186.d: An unaccompanied flute piece evoking Balinese gamelan: meditative, modal and atmospheric, with subtle colour and breath control.

p0187.d: An unaccompanied flute piece inspired by Chinese landscape: spacious, meditative lines with bends and colours suggesting the shakuhachi or dizi.
p0187.rw: Evocative, beautiful; needs control and colour

p0189.d: An atmospheric flute piece drawing on East Asian sounds: contemplative and spare, focused on colour, line and breath.

p0190.d: Pastoral French piece for flute and piano: a languid, sensuous opening giving way to lively, rhythmic music and brilliant passagework. Colourful and idiomatic, with plenty of fast tonguing.
p0190.rw: Idiomatic French favourite; colourful and rewarding

p0191.d: Short unaccompanied flute piece in free, improvisatory style: fluid arabesques, wide range and rapid flourishes contrasting with slow, evocative lines. Demands sure rhythm and tonal colour without piano support.
p0191.rw: Popular solo showcase of colour and flexibility

p0192.d: Short unaccompanied flute piece in free, improvisatory style: fluid arabesques, wide range and rapid flourishes contrasting with slow, evocative lines. Demands sure rhythm and tonal colour without piano support.
p0192.rw: Popular solo showcase of colour and flexibility

p0230.d: The graceful opening movement of Eldin Burton's Sonatina: a lilting, gently syncopated tune with jazzy American harmonies and fluent, light passagework. Charming and idiomatic.

p0231.d: Eldin Burton's flute Sonatina: a graceful, lightly jazzy Allegretto, a tender Andantino and a brisk, sparkling finale. Accessible American neo-romantic writing that suits the flute well.

p0238.d: Carter's unaccompanied flute piece inspired by Petrarch: contrasting registers and characters juxtaposed in fragmented, complex rhythms. Highly modernist and exacting.
p0238.rw: Major modern solo; demanding rhythm and control

p0239.d: Casella's two-part piece for flute: a gentle, lilting Sicilienne followed by an ironic, brilliant Burlesque with snappy rhythms and fast tonguing.
p0239.rw: Witty, colourful contrast; a flute favourite

p0247.d: Chaminade's single-movement Concertino: a lyrical, sweeping main theme, a reflective middle section and a brilliant cadenza and finish. Elegant, French and very flute-friendly.

p0263.d: Variations on 'Non più mesta' from Rossini's La Cenerentola for flute and piano, attributed to the young Chopin: a lyrical theme and increasingly brilliant variations.

p0264.d: A transcription of Chopin's melancholy B minor waltz: a wistful, singing melody with expressive rubato and a brighter middle section.

p0265.d: Ian Clarke's hypnotic flute piece built on a repeating, trance-like piano pattern, with a soaring melody and contemporary effects such as note bending. Atmospheric and moody.

p0267.d: Ian Clarke's evocative flute and piano piece, opening atmospherically and building to a lively dance with contemporary techniques and rhythmic drive.
p0267.rw: Popular modern piece with colour and drive

p0269.d: An atmospheric contemporary flute piece by Ian Clarke, with flowing lines and modern colour. Details not well known to me.

p0270.d: Valerie Coleman's unaccompanied flute piece inspired by Haitian heritage and family: rhythmic Caribbean-influenced music with lyrical passages and contemporary techniques.

p0274.d: Copland's three-movement Duo for flute and piano: an open, pastoral opening, a poignant slow movement and a lively, rhythmic finale in Copland's American style.

p0280.d: Dalbavie's flute concerto, written for Emmanuel Pahud: shimmering orchestral colour and extended virtuoso flute writing in a spectral-influenced style.

p0282.d: Damase's sonata for flute and piano: an elegant, witty French neo-classical work with lyrical lines and sparkling fast movements.

p0287.d: Two short unaccompanied pieces in Maxwell Davies's modernist idiom, demanding rhythmic precision, wide-ranging lines and a confident, varied tone without piano support.

p0292.d: Short, haunting solo for unaccompanied flute portraying Pan's lament, built on a sinuous chromatic melody. Technically modest but needs tonal colour, dynamic control and a sense of improvised freedom.
p0292.rw: Iconic flute solo; pure artistry, no piano needed

p0300.d: A melodic study in scherzo-and-trio form: a nimble, articulated outer section framing a more lyrical trio. A good test of clean finger technique and tonguing within musical phrasing.

p0301.d: A brilliant 19th-century French flute concert solo: operatic slow introduction and lyrical themes leading to dazzling variations-style passagework and fast articulation.

p0305.d: An early solo flute work by the extended-techniques pioneer, exploring multiphonics, timbral shading and resonance in a meditative, atmospheric sound world.
p0305.rw: Strong for players fluent in extended techniques

p0306.d: A groovy, blues-inflected solo by Robert Dick, mixing jazz-style riffs with extended techniques such as singing-while-playing and multiphonics. Fun, rhythmic and demanding.

p0308.d: A Hungarian/Romanian-flavoured fantasy in the virtuoso 19th-century style: a soulful slow introduction followed by dazzling folk-dance variations with rapid tonguing and runs.

p0309.d: A Hungarian/Romanian-flavoured fantasy in the virtuoso 19th-century style: a soulful slow introduction followed by dazzling folk-dance variations with rapid tonguing and runs.

p0310.d: A gentle, rocking lullaby with a simple singing melody over a lilting accompaniment. Short and lyrical, testing tone quality, legato and breath control.

p0311.d: Doppler's best-known work: a brooding, improvisatory slow introduction in gypsy style followed by a fiery, accelerating csárdás-like dance with brilliant passagework.
p0311.rw: Flute favourite; drama and dazzle combined

p0312.d: Doppler's best-known work: a brooding, improvisatory slow introduction in gypsy style followed by a fiery, accelerating csárdás-like dance with brilliant passagework.
p0312.rw: Flute favourite; drama and dazzle combined

p0315.d: A compact, sparkling three-section work (Allegretto, Andante, Animé) combining lyrical, Ravelian slow music with a dazzling cadenza and fast, rhythmically intricate finale.

p0341.d: A short Paris Conservatoire test piece: a long-breathed, sensuous Cantabile and a brilliant, scampering Presto. Combines lyrical control with dazzling articulation.

p0342.d: A short Paris Conservatoire test piece: a long-breathed, sensuous Cantabile and a brilliant, scampering Presto. Combines lyrical control with dazzling articulation.

p0353.d: A Paris Conservatoire test piece: a serene, lyrical Andantino followed by a sparkling Allegro of fast articulation and runs. Elegant French style with a brilliant finish.
p0353.rw: French flute classic; elegant and brilliant

p0364.d: Feld's flute concerto: a neoclassical work with driving rhythms, bright virtuosic passagework and a lyrical slow movement. Highly idiomatic and brilliant.

p0372.d: A contemporary flute piece published by Foxy Sounds; character inferred only from title and exam level.

p0378.d: Françaix's witty neoclassical divertimento: crisp, playful movements full of quick articulation, humour and Parisian charm, with lyrical interludes.

p0384.d: Japanese solo flute piece inspired by Noh theatre; sparse, intense phrases with breathy sounds, pitch bends and dramatic dynamics. Demands total control of tone and silence.
p0384.rw: Classic modern solo; strong communicators shine

p0386.d: An unaccompanied flute set of variations on the waltz once attributed to Beethoven (actually Schubert's). Charming Romantic tune decorated with increasingly brilliant runs and articulation.
p0386.rw: Useful articulation study with genuine charm

p0388.d: A 19th-century Italian operatic fantasy on themes from Ricci's opera, played from bar 89: tuneful melody followed by brilliant variations and runs.
p0388.rw: Showy and tuneful; bel canto flair rewarded

p0389.d: A French salon favourite: a tender, singing Andante followed by a quicksilver scherzo with rapid tonguing. Short, charming and brilliant.
p0389.rw: Charming contrast; shows tone and tonguing

p0391.d: A French Conservatoire-style fantasy with a dreamy, improvisatory opening and a dazzling, playful fast section. Colourful and idiomatic.
p0391.rw: Idiomatic French showpiece with real charm

p0392.d: A Paris Conservatoire-style piece: a hushed, atmospheric nocturne leading to a light, glittering scherzando. Elegant and colourful.
p0392.rw: Much-loved French staple; shows tone and agility

p0396.d: Gaubert's last flute sonata: elegant French writing with a flowing opening, a gentle, songful slow movement and a sparkling finale. Refined rather than flashy, needing poise and colour.
p0396.rw: Elegant French sonata; rewards refined tone

p0404.d: A cheerful mid-18th-century flute concerto (attribution to Gluck is doubtful): galant melodies, clear forms and light passagework.
p0404.rw: Pleasant but rarely chosen at diploma level

p0406.d: Three charming French pieces: a lively Allegretto, a tender Idylle and a famously sparkling Valse. Melodic and flattering to the flute.

p0413.d: A lively contemporary flute piece; judging by its title and context, energetic and rhythmic with crisp articulation.

p0423.d: Griffes's atmospheric Poem: shimmering, exotic harmonies, a haunting slow melody and a lively dance-like central section. A major American flute work.
p0423.rw: Cornerstone of the repertoire; colourful and rewarding

p0424.d: Griffes's atmospheric Poem: shimmering, exotic harmonies, a haunting slow melody and a lively dance-like central section. A major American flute work.
p0424.rw: Cornerstone of the repertoire; colourful and rewarding

p0428.d: An early Gubaidulina piece for flute and piano: rustic, energetic and spiky, with driving rhythms and sharp contrasts.

p0430.d: Elegant flute variations in Belle Époque style on a Mozart theme: graceful, witty and brilliant by turns.

p0431.d: A solo flute piece by American composer Adolphus Hailstork; judging by the title, free and soaring, with agile flights of virtuosic writing.

p0432.d: Handel's B minor flute sonata: a noble, expressive Largo leads into lively, dancing movements. Clean Baroque style with ornamentation.

p0434.d: Handel's E minor flute sonata: an expressive Baroque sonata with a grave opening, brisk allegros and dance-like finale. Ornamentation adds style.

p0437.d: Harty's Irish fantasy for flute: a lilting folk-like lament leading to a vivid jig, evoking a street fiddler. Charming and evocative.

p0449.d: A jazz-influenced flute piece in cool-jazz style: laid-back, swung melody with bluesy inflections and rhythmic syncopation.

p0455.d: Higdon's breathless solo flute piece depicting violence in cities: relentless, rapid-fire passagework and percussive articulation.
p0455.rw: Intense and gripping; a real tour de force

p0458.d: The opening of Hindemith's flute sonata: a cheerful, neoclassical movement with lyrical lines and crisp interplay with the piano.

p0460.d: The slow movement of Hindemith's flute sonata: grave and expressive, with long, searching melodic lines over austere harmonies.

p0462.d: Hindemith's flute sonata (1936): a cheerful, neoclassical first movement, a grave slow movement, and a lively finale ending in a march. Clear-cut, contrapuntal and rhythmically crisp.

p0474.d: A short avant-garde solo flute piece by Heinz Holliger: fragmented gestures, extreme dynamics and extended techniques.

p0477.d: Unaccompanied flute piece written for a dancer: a slow, hazy opening gives way to a skittish, capricious goat dance. Short, colourful and full of character.
p0477.rw: Flute classic; big character payoff in three minutes

p0478.d: Solo flute piece evoking the Native American flute-player figure: free, chant-like lines, bends and percussive effects build to a driving, rhythmic close.
p0478.rw: Popular modern solo; atmospheric and engaging

p0481.d: French flute-and-piano showpiece in the Paris Conservatoire style: a lyrical, perfumed opening followed by a sparkling, virtuosic fast section.
p0481.rw: Elegant French concours piece; shows tone and fingers

p0483.d: Ibert's three-movement concerto: a perpetual-motion Allegro, a tender, long-breathed Andante and a brilliant, technically fierce finale. A cornerstone of the flute repertoire.

p0484.d: Two-movement sonatina for flute and piano: a playful, light-footed Animé and a graceful, witty Tendre. Charming French neoclassical writing that needs a light touch.
p0484.rw: Witty, charming and rewarding for a light touch

y00336.d: Mozart's Flute Concerto No. 1 in G, K. 313 (1778). Bright and virtuosic with demanding cadenzas.
